title: The energy cascade and Kolmogorov's hypotheses: which small-scale statistics are universal, and when
status: reviewed and locally validated; passes 1-9 complete; gate 6b passed round 2 (0 blocking)
transcript_provenance: Local machine transcription (faster-whisper small.en); not publisher captions
source_uncertainties: The Module 06 'Source' slide is shown for less than 30 s; one frame was extracted at 84 s of Lecture 26 (helper file outside the repository). It names Pope, Turbulent Flows (Cambridge University Press, 2000). No page, equation or value of that book is used.

L26 about 1500 s: the speech recognition gives 'epsilon is independent of u'; the slide (f0054) reads 'consistent with experimental observations in free shear flows where epsilon is independent of nu'. The chapter follows the slide.

L26 f0054 board note writes tau_0 = u_0/l_0 (and the speech says 'tau 0 is u0 over L0'); the slide definition tau(l) = l/u(l) (f0028) gives l_0/u_0. The chapter uses the slide definition and states the correction.

L26 about 1155-1227 s: the speech says 'u prime is two-third K' at 1207 s and 'two-third k to the half' at 1190 s and 1222 s; the board (f0041) and the slide (f0028) both write u' = (2k/3)^(1/2). The chapter follows the slide; no correction of the lecture is involved.

The factors l_EI = l_0/6 and l_DI = 60 eta are called arbitrary for now by the lecture, with the reason deferred to later modules. Not verified against any source; the chapter labels them nominal and makes every derived threshold (10.17) and Figure 10.1 conditional on them.

Slide f0012 states epsilon approximately equal to T_EI without a condition. The conditions (negligible large-scale dissipation; stationarity or fast small scales) and the estimate (10.10) are teaching constructions of this chapter, not lecture material.
The slides write the ratios with Re; the board derivation (L27 f0051, L28 f0020) uses u_0 l_0/nu, which the chapter writes Re_0 (the slide symbol of f0028).
L27 about 1301-1305 s: the speech recognition gives 'less than lei over 8'; the slide (f0040) reads |y| < l_EI/eta.

Kolmogorov 1941 translation, p. 10, prints the flow time scale as 'T = U/L'; the chapter does not quote it and describes the condition in words (time dimensions small compared with the time scale of the flow).
Kolmogorov 1941, p. 12: the translation writes lambda for the Kolmogorov length; the chapter states the mapping to eta.

Schumacher, Sreenivasan and Yeung: checked on the arXiv preprint (nlin/0210010v1, pp. 1-2); journal pagination (Phys. Fluids 15, 84-90, from Crossref) not checked page by page. The Shen and Warhaft result is cited only as reported by them.
McComb et al. 2015: the attributions to Batchelor (1953) and Sreenivasan (1984) are theirs (accepted manuscript p. 2); neither original was opened.
Identification of McComb et al.'s R_L (rms velocity, integral scale) with the jet's Re_0 (energy-containing size l_0) is an assumption stated in the text.
Exercise 6 uses an assumed chi = 0.025; Kolmogorov 1962 gives no value for its constant (written k there), and none is cited.
Timestamps are section anchors from local speech-recognition segment times; they locate topic changes to within a few seconds.

sections.section: The objects of the chapter and the running case
sections.lecture_material: Symbols u(l), tau(l), l_0, u_0, Re, Re_0 from the slides.
sections.teaching_construction: Formal model of flow scales and eddy scales; continuation of the air jet of chapters 6-8 with the atmospheric layer of chapter 5 as contrast; notation Re_0 versus Re(l).

sections.section: Turbulent motions span a range of sizes that widens with the Reynolds number
sections.lecture_material: Laminar flow has one characteristic length (1 cm jet example); turbulent motions range from the flow width delta to much smaller scales that shrink as Re increases; continuum still valid; Re 1e5 versus 1e10 illustration.
sections.teaching_construction: Factor 5.6e3 from Re^(-3/4) with its assumptions; Knudsen number from chapter 6.

sections.section: Richardson's energy cascade: inviscid transfer and viscous dissipation
sections.lecture_material: Richardson (1922) cascade idea; production at the largest scales; transfer by inviscid processes; dissipation by viscosity; Navier-Stokes inertia term breaks up large scales, viscous term dominant at small scales; Kolmogorov (1941) quantified the picture.
sections.research_extension: Richardson 1922, p. 66: 'big whirls have little whirls...' in the context of cumulus convection and a single eddy coefficient.
sections.teaching_construction: Proof (10.1)-(10.2) that inertia and pressure terms conserve energy in a periodic box; triad identity (10.3); statement that neither proves direction or locality of transfer.

sections.section: Eddies, their scales and the Reynolds number of the largest eddies
sections.lecture_material: Re = U L/nu known before the flow; eddy definition; u(l), tau(l) = l/u(l); l_0 comparable to L; u_0 of order u' = (2k/3)^(1/2) comparable to U; Re_0 = u_0 l_0/nu large, viscous effects negligible.
sections.teaching_construction: Origin of the factor 2/3 via (8.25); local flow scales in a developing jet (factor 28); Re_0^(-1) = 7.3e-5 via (5.17).

sections.section: The dissipation rate is set by the largest eddies
sections.lecture_material: Richardson's notion of unstable eddies; cascade continues until Re small; epsilon ~ u_0^2/tau_0 = u_0^3/l_0 set by the first step; consistent with observations in free shear flows where epsilon is independent of nu.
sections.research_extension: McComb et al. 2015: epsilon = C_eps U^3/L (p. 2), Batchelor 1953 and Sreenivasan 1984 attributions (p. 2), C_eps = C_eps,inf + C/R_L with 0.468 +/- 0.006 and 18.9 +/- 1.3 up to R_L = 5875 (p. 1).
sections.teaching_construction: Exact dimensional form (10.6); pipeline argument for why the first step sets the rate; running-case C_eps = 0.4694 and 0.3 % change per factor 2 in nu; correction of the board tau_0.

sections.lecture_material: Two questions (size of smallest eddies; trend of u(l), tau(l)); three hypotheses premised on decreasing u(l), tau(l); large eddies anisotropic and affected by BCs; directional bias lost; hypothesis of local isotropy at sufficiently high Re for l << l_0; 'sufficiently high Re' emphasized.
sections.research_extension: Kolmogorov 1941, Definitions 1-2 (pp. 9-10), likelihood statement, domain conditions, cannot be rigorously proved, Taylor isotropy confirmed only for grid turbulence (p. 10). Schumacher, Sreenivasan, Yeung (arXiv pp. 1-2): skewness of du/dy falls off less steeply than 1/R_lambda; hyperskewness not perceptibly diminished at R_lambda 1000; Shen and Warhaft seventh moment increases; their reading that this need not imply persistent anisotropy.
sections.teaching_construction: Reflection proof (10.8) that odd moments of a transverse derivative vanish under local isotropy; application to the jet.

sections.section: A demarcation length and the loss of the flow's geometry
sections.lecture_material: l_EI ~ l_0/6 (nominal); anisotropic large and isotropic small eddies; geometry of large eddies lost; universality; zoom-in illustration jet versus channel versus cylinder.
sections.teaching_construction: Running-case l_EI values; distinction between pictures and statistics.

sections.section: Transfer, dissipation and the first similarity hypothesis
sections.lecture_material: Two dominant processes: transfer rate T_EI and viscous dissipation; epsilon ~ T_EI; first similarity hypothesis; Kolmogorov scales; identities Re_eta = 1 and epsilon = nu (u_eta/eta)^2 = nu/tau_eta^2; Kolmogorov scales characterize the dissipative eddies.
sections.research_extension: Kolmogorov 1941, p. 12: first hypothesis of similarity in his words.
sections.teaching_construction: Small-scale energy budget (10.9) for homogeneous turbulence, with the large-scale dissipation bounded by Re(l_EI)^-1 = 8.0e-4 for the jet, (transport term needed and not estimated for the jet) and departure estimate (10.10) with decaying-grid-turbulence value 0.2; universal-function form (10.11); exact mean-square strain (10.13) and running-case value 1.65e3 1/s.

sections.section: In Kolmogorov units the small scales of different flows are statistically identical
sections.lecture_material: y = (x - x_0)/eta, w(y) = [U(x,t_0) - U(x_0,t_0)]/u_eta; statistically isotropic and identical for |y| < l_EI/eta; statistically similar, identical when scaled.
sections.research_extension: Kolmogorov 1941, p. 9 (moving coordinates) and p. 12 (eqs. 15-18, rescaling to unit viscosity and dissipation).
sections.teaching_construction: Statement in terms of the N-point PDF (8.23); jet versus ABL conversions (127 eta and 3.0 eta per cm; u_eta ratio 41; |y| = 20 lengths; bound ratio 240).

sections.section: The ratios of the smallest to the largest scales
sections.lecture_material: Ratios from the definitions and epsilon ~ u_0^3/l_0; derivation of eta/l_0 ~ Re^(-3/4).
sections.teaching_construction: Back-reference to (5.18) without re-derivation; constants C_eps kept; statement that the ratios need the empirical scaling; running-case values.

sections.section: The ratios of the smallest to the largest scales (continued)
sections.lecture_material: Recap of the first similarity hypothesis and identities; derivations of u_eta/u_0 ~ Re^(-1/4) and tau_eta/tau_0 ~ Re^(-1/2); smallest scales very small compared with largest; separation widens with Re.
Range l_0 >> l >> eta; Re of these eddies large; second similarity hypothesis (determined by epsilon, independent of nu).
sections.research_extension: Kolmogorov 1941, p. 12: second hypothesis of similarity in his words (lower bound only) and its footnote; p. 13, eqs. 22-23: B_dd(r) ~ C eps^(2/3) r^(2/3) with an absolute constant.
sections.teaching_construction: Unique exponents (10.16) with undetermined constant; consistency of the two hypotheses (Phi(x) -> C_u x^(1/3)).

sections.section: The energy-containing range, the inertial subrange and the dissipation range
sections.lecture_material: l_DI = 60 eta (nominal); universal equilibrium range split into inertial subrange and dissipation range; energy-containing range l_0/6 < l < 6 l_0; slide figure of eddy-size ranges.
sections.teaching_construction: Figure 10.1 computed for jet and ABL; existence condition (10.17) with thresholds 2.56e3 and 5.5e4 (C_eps = 1), 3.30e3 and 7.1e4 (C_eps = 0.468); jet 0.55 decades, ABL 2.9 decades; sensitivity to the nominal factors.

sections.section: Velocity and time scales in the inertial subrange
sections.lecture_material: u(l) = (eps l)^(1/3) = u_eta (l/eta)^(1/3) ~ u_0 (l/l_0)^(1/3); tau(l) = (l^2/eps)^(1/3) = tau_eta (l/eta)^(2/3) ~ tau_0 (l/l_0)^(2/3); board elimination of nu; u(l) and tau(l) decrease as l decreases.
sections.teaching_construction: Constant-transfer identity (10.20); end-value identities; eddy Reynolds number (10.21) with Re(l_DI) = 235; running-case velocities and times; gradient scaling l^(-2/3).

sections.section: Executable range calculator with identity checks
sections.teaching_construction: NumPy program: exponents of (10.16) and group of (10.11) from dimension matrices; scales and ranges for jet and ABL; 12 assertions (6 identities per flow) plus 4 threshold assertions; bisection for (10.17); C_eps(R_L); failure test.

sections.section: What the hypotheses establish and what they do not
sections.research_extension: Kolmogorov 1962 (pp. 82-85): Landau's objection, log-normal epsilon_r with variance A + 9k log(L/r), refined hypotheses, moments (10.22) with macrostructure-dependent C_p. Schumacher et al. (shear-flow anisotropy); Yeung, Sreenivasan, Pope 2018 via chapter 5.
sections.teaching_construction: Classification of each statement (picture, empirical result, hypothesis, dimensional consequence, nominal value); finite-Re limits for the two flows.

sections.research_extension: Exercise 4 uses Kolmogorov 1941 eq. 14 via chapter 5; exercise 6 uses Kolmogorov 1962 eq. 10.
sections.teaching_construction: Six original exercises with full solutions: derive, compute, check an assumption, counterexample, judge a design, derive and compute.

references.title: Richardson 1922, Weather Prediction by Numerical Process (Cambridge University Press)
references.supports: p. 66, section 4/8/0: 'We realize thus that: big whirls have little whirls that feed on their velocity, and little whirls have lesser whirls and so on to viscosity -- in the molecular sense.' Context: cumulus updrafts; a single coefficient for eddies of all sizes.

references.title: Kolmogorov 1941, The local structure of turbulence (English translation, Proc. R. Soc. Lond. A 434, 1991)
references.supports: Definitions 1-2 (local homogeneity, local isotropy; narrower and wider than Taylor's isotropy); moving coordinates; isotropy confirmed for grid turbulence, far approximation otherwise; local isotropy 'rather likely' in small domains away from boundaries; cannot be rigorously proved; first and second hypotheses of similarity and footnote; lambda = nu^(3/4)/eps^(1/4); rescaling to nu' = eps' = 1; B_dd(r) ~ C eps^(2/3) r^(2/3).
references.page_checked: p. 9 (PDF p. 2); p. 10 (PDF p. 3); p. 12 (PDF p. 5, page image viewed); p. 13 (PDF p. 6, page image viewed)

references.title: Kolmogorov 1962, A refinement of previous hypotheses concerning the local structure of turbulence (J. Fluid Mech. 13, 82-85)
references.supports: p. 82: Landau's objection (variation of dissipation should increase without limit with L/l), Oboukhov's refinement; p. 83: epsilon_r averaged over a sphere of radius r, log-normal, variance A(x,t) + 9k log L/r, k universal, A depends on macrostructure; modified hypotheses; p. 84, eq. (10): moments of |Delta_dd(r)|^p = C_p(x,t) (r eps)^(p/3) (L/r)^(k p(p-3)/2); pp. 84-85: hypotheses restated. Volume and pages confirmed by Crossref.
references.page_checked: pp. 82-85 (PDF pp. 1-4); pp. 83-84 page images viewed; copy https://courses.physics.ucsd.edu/2019/Spring/physics235/Kolmogorov%2062-Enter%20Intermittency.pdf

references.title: McComb, Berera, Yoffe, Linkmann 2015, Energy transfer and dissipation in forced isotropic turbulence (Phys. Rev. E 91, 043013)
references.supports: p. 1: C_eps = C_eps,inf + C/R_L, C = 18.9 +/- 1.3, C_eps,inf = 0.468 +/- 0.006, DNS of forced isotropic turbulence up to R_L = 5875; p. 2: epsilon = C_eps U^3/L with U rms velocity and L integral scale; Batchelor (1953) evidence of a constant; Sreenivasan (1984) constant in grid turbulence for R_lambda above about 50 (their attributions).
references.page_checked: accepted-manuscript pp. 1, 2 (same as PDF pages); journal pagination not checked

references.title: Schumacher, Sreenivasan, Yeung 2003, Derivative moments in turbulent shear flows (Phys. Fluids 15, 84-90; DOI 10.1063/1.1524627)
references.supports: p. 1: local isotropy demands zero odd moments of transverse derivatives; R_lambda and lambda definitions; skewness data roll off less steeply than the inverse power from linear shear dependence; abstract: non-vanishing odd moments do not necessarily imply persistent anisotropy. p. 2: hyperskewness does not diminish perceptibly even at R_lambda about 1000; Shen and Warhaft seventh moment increased with R_lambda.
references.page_checked: arXiv preprint nlin/0210010v1 pp. 1-2 (PDF pp. 1-2); journal pagination not checked
